items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Cecil told me, -- and the trombone player, Clinton Green, to meet him the next day and he'd take us down, because he had joined. He took us down there and we joined.

ctx.x: Cecil told me, -- because we were working with Honey

Potter at the time, Cecil told me, -- and the trombone player, Clinton Green, to meet him the next day and he'd take us down, because he had joined. He took us down there and we joined. Two dollars to join 802. Now it costs you $75. Two dollars and they put a little sheet in front of you and say, play that. That was nothing.

And, of course, when I joined Fletcher I was with the union. We were all union men, and Fletcher and Duke and all like that. 802 right straight through. I was just going to say how good those fellows were to me, those older men. And all through my career, I was always with older men. Now, I'm on myself now, because all of them are gone.
